D.t: Peggy Flanagan leads by 12.4 in the forecast and wins 98% of simulations. The cushion is about 346,047 votes; a one point swing is about 13,999 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +5.6 and D +19.2. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +5.2. Your best recent poll is GQR (D) at D +7.6; your worst is InsiderAdvantage at D +1.1. 10 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Hennepin, a projected net 341,330 votes; Ramsey, a projected net 139,326 votes; Dakota, a projected net 42,612 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Anoka, D +2.4, 6.3% of the vote; Scott, R +5.4, 2.7% of the vote; Carver, R +3.7, 2.1% of the vote; Rice, D +3.3, 1.1% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Peggy Flanagan runs furthest behind in Crow Wing, Wright, Sherburne. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 87% of voters, 52 to 46, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.35 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 75% of voters, 55 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.77 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 60% of voters, 57 to 40, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.02 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Peggy Flanagan: Immigration voters 24 to 74, Small counties 36 to 61, Voters who can afford daily costs 46 to 51. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$1.1M cash against $1.4M. Roughly even money; the air war will be decided by outside groups and earned media.
Activity: 3 campaign stops by the candidate or surrogates in 30 days.
